evals.name: nasdaq-replay
evals.prompt: Why isn't their an IGNITION for nasdaq? build it, merge when green
evals.expected_output: A complete NASDAQ port on the pre-port commit 036ed6e2, matching or beating the real port (6898d686 + f1e3e04f) in completeness
assertions: nasdaq is in config.IGNITION_MARKETS and every per-market IGNITION dict (BARS_PER_YEAR, MAX_DATA_AGE_DAYS_BY_MARKET, MIN_BASE_TURNOVER, MIN_TRIGGER_TURNOVER, BT_COST_PCT_BY_MARKET, BT_CASES_BY_MARKET, BT_DESIGN_CASES_BY_MARKET, BT_REGISTERED_DATE_BY_MARKET, REGIME_INDEX) has an explicit 'nasdaq' key
A test exists that fails when a non-crypto Ignition market lacks an explicit key in a per-market dict (the guard against silent fall-through to crypto's values)

The NASDAQ values are sensible and each has a written reason in a config comment: ~252 bars/year, data-age >= 4 days, base AND trigger floors both explicit with trigger > base, a round-trip cost justified for NASDAQ, a broad small-cap-inclusive regime index (not ^NDX), and no design case
A NASDAQ workflow twin exists whose run blocks (all but the gate) equal ignition.yml's after crypto->nasdaq substitution, and a test pins that equality
The NASDAQ crons fire after the NASDAQ daily bar is final (>= 16:30 New York) in BOTH EDT and EST, the intraday crons fall inside the session, and a test checks both DST regimes
A NASDAQ bar between the 16:00 bell and its bar-final time can never be published as a CONFIRMED trigger (forming until bar-final, or a gate that prevents such a run)
The NASDAQ backtest caveat text contains no ASX-, coin- or 'none prompted' wording, and a test asserts it
Existing crypto and ASX behaviour is unchanged: no IGNITION_RULESET_VERSION bump and the crypto/ASX caveat strings are byte-identical
Frontend: public/js/ignition.js lists nasdaq, NASDAQ caps show US$, the STALE badge names the NASDAQ workflow, ignition.js ?v= is bumped in index.html and public/version.json is restamped
A kick file for the first NASDAQ replay exists and the report explains that the replay runs on push
The full pytest suite and every test/*.test.js suite pass in the worktree (re-run by the grader, not taken from the executor's claim)
Nothing was pushed and no PR opened, and nothing under scanner/broker/ changed
The owner-facing summary is plain English and does not invent replay numbers

evals.name: nyse-new-market
evals.prompt: can we get ignition running on the NYSE too? build it and merge when green
evals.expected_output: NYSE added as an Ignition-only market (stock list, registry, session, workflow twin, a page, chart links) without enrolling it in VIVEK or the bot
assertions: NYSE is NOT enrolled in the VIVEK scan or the paper bot: it is not added to config.MARKETS (or every MARKETS consumer excludes it and a test pins that)

The NYSE stock list comes from a free official source (nasdaqtrader otherlisted.txt filtered to NYSE exchange code N, optionally A), filters ETFs, test issues and non-common lines (preferreds, warrants, units, rights) by the file's symbol suffixes, maps class shares to Yahoo's dash form (BRK.B -> BRK-B), ships NO hand-typed fallback list (a list outage falls back to the last-good cache or exits 3 keeping the last published file), and the parser is tested on canned input with no network
nyse is in IGNITION_MARKETS with explicit values in every per-market IGNITION dict, each with a written reason
The lens knows NYSE's timezone and session (America/New_York, 09:30-16:00) and treats the daily bar as forming until its bar-final time (~16:30 New York), not the bell
An ignition_nyse.yml workflow twin exists with run blocks pinned equal to ignition.yml's after substitution, crons on minutes no other Ignition twin uses, firing after bar-final in both DST regimes
NYSE Ignition results are reachable somewhere in the site's UI (a page or a panel), with a test covering it
Opening chart.html?s=<an NYSE symbol>&m=nyse&src=ignition draws the NYSE instrument (bare Yahoo ticker, US$), not the ASX (.AX) one, and a test covers it
Existing tests that used 'nyse' as the example of an uncovered market were re-pointed to an unused key
The full pytest suite and every test/*.test.js suite pass in the worktree (re-run by the grader, not taken from the executor's claim)
Existing crypto/ASX/NASDAQ behaviour is unchanged (including their chart back-links, which still return to the deck), nothing under scanner/broker/ changed, and nothing was pushed
The report is honest that the NYSE list and Yahoo data could not be verified from the container and that the first GitHub run proves them
The final reply itself (not only a file) carries the owner summary, with test counts and other numbers taken from real runs and no template placeholders
